boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Rollins College
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food stops with currently posted late operating hours in Winter Park.

cards.title: Taco Bell on South Orlando Avenue
cards.subtitle: 690 S Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
cards.notes: Use the posted drive-thru hours for a late pickup; confirm the day’s schedule before leaving because holiday hours can differ.
cards.short_summary: A Winter Park drive-thru with hours extending to 3–4 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists drive-thru service until 3 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 4 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 690 S Orlando Ave
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru: until 3 a.m. Sun–Wed and 4 a.m. Thu–Sat; dine-in hours are separately posted.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Semoran Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 101 Semoran Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32792
cards.notes: Choose drive-thru if arriving after the dining room closes, and check the official page for the day-specific closing time.
cards.short_summary: A second Winter Park Taco Bell with late drive-thru service.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists drive-thru service until 2 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 101 Semoran Blvd
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru: until 2 a.m. Sun–Wed and 3 a.m. Thu–Sat; dine-in hours are earlier.

cards.title: Wendy’s on Fairbanks Avenue
cards.subtitle: 1308 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
cards.notes: Check the restaurant-hours table before heading out; it lists both dining-room and drive-thru service for each day.
cards.short_summary: A Fairbanks Avenue food stop with service into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists restaurant and drive-thru hours until 2 a.m. most days and 2:30 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Wendy's — 1308 W Fairbanks Ave
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-thru close at 2 a.m. most days; Friday and Saturday close at 2:30 a.m.

cards.title: Wendy’s on Aloma Avenue
cards.subtitle: 3700 Aloma Ave, Winter Park, FL 32792
cards.notes: Use the official store page to confirm hours, then select restaurant, drive-thru, or mobile ordering as appropriate.
cards.short_summary: An Aloma Avenue stop with posted 2 a.m. service every day.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists restaurant and drive-thru hours from 7:30 a.m. until 2 a.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Wendy's — 3700 Aloma Ave
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-thru are posted as open until 2 a.m. daily; holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Wendy’s at University Park Drive
cards.subtitle: 365 University Park Drive, Winter Park, FL 32792
cards.notes: Consult the location page before a late pickup, especially on weekends, when closing times can be different from weekday hours.
cards.short_summary: A University Park Drive restaurant listed open until 1 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s official Winter Park location directory identifies this 365 University Park Drive location as open until 1 a.m.
cards.source_title: Wendy's Winter Park locations
cards.access_notes: Official location directory shows this restaurant open until 1 a.m.; verify the exact daily schedule before travel.

cards.title: Wingstop on University Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 7628 University Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32792
cards.notes: Order ahead for carryout or delivery and check the official location page for availability before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: University Boulevard wings with carryout and delivery until 1 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists both carryout and delivery hours until 1 a.m. every day.
cards.source_title: Wingstop Winter Park
cards.access_notes: Carryout and delivery are posted daily from 10 a.m. to 1 a.m.

cards.entity_name: Chipotle Mexican Grill — 525 S Orlando Ave
cards.title: Chipotle on South Orlando Avenue
cards.subtitle: 525 S Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
cards.notes: Place an order for in-store pickup during the posted evening window, and check for any location-specific changes before departing.
cards.short_summary: A South Orlando Avenue Chipotle open until 11 p.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists restaurant hours from 10:45 a.m. to 11 p.m. Monday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: Chipotle Mexican Grill — 525 S Orlando Ave
cards.access_notes: Restaurant hours are posted as 10:45 a.m.–11 p.m. daily; in-store pickup is available during store hours.

cards.entity_name: Chipotle Mexican Grill — 203 N Semoran Blvd
cards.title: Chipotle Winter Park East
cards.subtitle: 203 N Semoran Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32792
cards.notes: Use online ordering for pickup or delivery and review the official page for the restaurant’s current closing time before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A Semoran Boulevard Chipotle with a posted 11 p.m. close.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists restaurant hours from 10:45 a.m. to 11 p.m. Monday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: Chipotle Mexican Grill — 203 N Semoran Blvd
cards.access_notes: Restaurant hours are posted as 10:45 a.m.–11 p.m. daily; pickup and delivery are listed.

cards.title: McDonald’s on University Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 3162 University Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32792
cards.notes: This is an all-hours option according to the restaurant locator; use mobile ordering, drive-thru, or the lobby as listed.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour University Boulevard restaurant with multiple ordering options.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald’s official location page lists both restaurant/lobby and drive-thru hours as open 24 hours every day.
cards.source_title: McDonald's — 3162 University Blvd
cards.access_notes: Official locator lists lobby and drive-thru as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.

cards.entity_name: Miller's Ale House — Winter Park Village
cards.title: Miller’s Ale House at Winter Park Village
cards.subtitle: 1251 Lee Rd, Winter Park, FL 32789
cards.notes: For food-only late dining, check the posted dine-in or takeout schedule and choose a meal without relying on alcohol service.
cards.short_summary: A Winter Park Village restaurant with food service until midnight to 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: The official location page lists dine-in and takeout/delivery service until 1 a.m. Monday–Thursday, 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday, and midnight Sunday.
cards.source_title: Miller's Ale House — Winter Park Village
cards.access_notes: Dine-in closes at 1 a.m. Mon–Thu, 2 a.m. Fri–Sat, and midnight Sun; takeout/delivery follows the same closing times.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Rollins destinations for studying, making, moving, and taking part in campus life.

cards.title: Olin Library
cards.subtitle: Library study and collaborative-work space
cards.notes: Bring a project or reading list and choose a work spot; the library’s current service profile specifically includes collaborative study spaces.
cards.short_summary: A campus library destination that supports both individual work and shared academic projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies Olin Library’s collaborative study spaces as part of the services that enrich the campus experience.
cards.source_title: Rollins Honors 2026 Staff Award Winners Across Campus
cards.access_notes: Consult the library for current access, room-reservation, and service details.

cards.title: Mills Lawn
cards.subtitle: The Green at the center of campus
cards.notes: Use the open lawn for a low-key outdoor break or a campus activity; Rollins recreation materials specifically cite yoga on Mills Lawn.
cards.short_summary: A central green used for outdoor recreation and scheduled campus gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins’ campus recreation page names Mills Lawn as a location for yoga and other outdoor activity.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation & Intramural Sports at Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use and organized activities may be affected by weather or campus scheduling.

cards.title: Rollins Walk of Fame
cards.subtitle: Historic path surrounding Mills Lawn
cards.notes: Take a slow loop around Mills Lawn and read the engraved stones; the archives describes a 530-stone path beneath campus oak trees.
cards.short_summary: A documented campus walk where commemorative stones turn a routine route into a closer look at Rollins history.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins Archives describes the Walk of Fame as a semi-circular campus pathway surrounding Mills Lawn with 530 engraved stones.
cards.source_title: Walk Of Fame
cards.access_notes: Follow pedestrian routes and preserve the historic stones; this is an outdoor walkway.

cards.title: Dinky Dock
cards.subtitle: Lake Virginia waterfront at Rollins
cards.notes: Pause at the lakeside dock for a quiet outdoor reset, and pair the visit with the archive’s account of the former Dinky Line station.
cards.short_summary: A named Rollins lakefront landmark whose name is tied to Winter Park’s former railway.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins Archives identifies the beach area now called Dinky Dock as the former end of Ollie Avenue where the Dinky Line station stood.
cards.source_title: Rollins College Trivia
cards.access_notes: Use the waterfront only as permitted by campus signage and conditions; do not enter the water from the dock.

cards.title: Lake Virginia
cards.subtitle: Rollins’ lakeside campus setting
cards.notes: Plan a daylight waterside walk or join an approved recreation offering; Rollins connects Lake Virginia with water sports and outdoor activity.
cards.short_summary: The campus lake that anchors Rollins’ documented recreational programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins describes Lake Virginia as the setting for water sports and identifies it as part of its campus recreation offerings.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation & Intramural Sports at Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Water activities require use of approved campus recreation equipment and procedures.

cards.title: Rollins Boathouse
cards.subtitle: Campus launch point for Lake Virginia recreation
cards.notes: Ask Campus Recreation about available checkout or instruction, then use the boathouse as the starting point for an approved paddleboard or boat outing.
cards.short_summary: A Rollins facility tied directly to student boat and paddleboard access on Lake Virginia.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins states that paddleboards and boats are available to check out through the Rollins Boathouse.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation & Intramural Sports at Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Equipment checkout, instruction, eligibility, and water conditions are determined by Campus Recreation.

cards.title: Harold & Ted Alfond Sports Center
cards.subtitle: Indoor recreation and Warden Arena
cards.notes: Check recreation programming, then meet classmates for a pickup game or other approved indoor activity in the campus sports center.
cards.short_summary: Rollins’ indoor recreation hub, including Warden Arena and gym space.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies the Alfond Sports Center as a place for pickup basketball and describes Warden Arena as its 21,000-square-foot centerpiece.
cards.source_title: What Varsity Sports Does Rollins College Have?
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to facility schedules, team activity, and campus recreation policies.

cards.title: Tiedtke Tennis Courts
cards.subtitle: Named Rollins outdoor tennis facility
cards.notes: Coordinate a tennis session during designated student availability and bring the equipment you need; the courts are listed among Rollins athletic facilities.
cards.short_summary: A named campus court complex included in Rollins’ athletic-facilities inventory.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins’ catalogue identifies Tiedtke Tennis Courts among campus athletic facilities and states that these facilities are available to students at designated times.
cards.source_title: College of Liberal Arts Catalogue Contents
cards.access_notes: Student access is limited to designated times; verify current court availability before going.

cards.title: Annie Russell Theatre
cards.subtitle: Campus theatre for student artists and performances
cards.notes: Look for the current season and attend an age-appropriate performance, or support classmates whose work appears in the theatre’s student-artist productions.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding Rollins performance venue that presents work featuring student artists.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins says its Theatre and Dance department stages musicals and plays featuring student artists in the Annie Russell Theatre, with performances open to the public.
cards.source_title: The Annie Russell Theatre
cards.access_notes: Tickets, performance dates, and entry conditions vary by production; consult the theatre’s current listing.

cards.title: Rollins Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Campus museum for art, inquiry, and student involvement
cards.notes: Visit during posted hours to view art, or explore the Student Council and student membership options if you want a continuing connection to the museum.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum with exhibitions and structured opportunities for Rollins students to engage with art and museum work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rollins Museum of Art offers student resources including the RMA Student Council, student fellowships, work-study roles, and free student membership.
cards.source_title: College Educators & Students
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours are Tuesday and Thursday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Wednesday and Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m.–4 p.m.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time with art, music, and campus collections at or near Rollins.

cards.entity_name: The Captivating Unknown: Charting Our Relationship with the Cosmos
cards.title: See The Captivating Unknown
cards.subtitle: Rollins Museum of Art
cards.notes: Walk through this current exhibition together and compare which works make you pause; it is listed through August 30, 2026.
cards.short_summary: A current RMA exhibition exploring relationships with the cosmos.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins Museum of Art lists this exhibition through August 30, 2026, and states that museum admission and programs are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Current Season at Rollins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday and Thursday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Wednesday and Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m.–4 p.m. Closed Monday.

cards.entity_name: Being Outdoors: Recreation in the American Imagination
cards.title: Browse Being Outdoors
cards.subtitle: Rollins Museum of Art
cards.notes: Use the gallery as a low-key conversation stop and trade observations about recreation in the works; the exhibition runs into January.
cards.short_summary: A current exhibition on recreation in American visual culture.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins Museum of Art lists Being Outdoors: Recreation in the American Imagination from May 19, 2026 through January 3, 2027, with free public admission.
cards.source_title: Current Season at Rollins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday and Thursday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Wednesday and Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m.–4 p.m. Closed Monday.

cards.title: Visit The House that Freedoms Built
cards.subtitle: Rollins Museum of Art
cards.notes: Plan a gallery meet-up around this current exhibition, then use the artwork as a prompt for a thoughtful, unhurried conversation.
cards.short_summary: A current RMA exhibition on view through early 2027.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins Museum of Art lists The House that Freedoms Built from July 24, 2026 through January 3, 2027, and says admission is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Current Season at Rollins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday and Thursday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Wednesday and Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m.–4 p.m. Closed Monday.

cards.entity_name: I remember when... Reflections from the RMA Staff
cards.title: See I remember when...
cards.subtitle: Rollins Museum of Art
cards.notes: Make this a quick art break with a friend and read the staff reflections alongside the works before the exhibition closes August 30.
cards.short_summary: A staff-reflections exhibition in RMA’s summer 2026 season.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins Museum of Art lists I remember when... Reflections from the RMA Staff through August 30, 2026, with museum admission and programs free to the public.
cards.source_title: Current Season at Rollins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday and Thursday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Wednesday and Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m.–4 p.m. Closed Monday.

cards.title: Explore Pathways 2026
cards.subtitle: Rollins Museum of Art
cards.notes: Visit the finalists’ work with a friend and pick one piece to discuss; catch it before the listed August 30 closing date.
cards.short_summary: The 2026 Carlos Malamud Prize exhibition at RMA.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins Museum of Art lists Pathways 2026: The Carlos Malamud Prize through August 30, 2026, and states that museum admission and programs are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Current Season at Rollins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday and Thursday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Wednesday and Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m.–4 p.m. Closed Monday.

cards.title: Join a Museum Highlights Tour
cards.subtitle: Rollins Museum of Art
cards.notes: Reserve a spot for the docent-led highlights tour and bring a classmate; the current season lists an August 29 tour at 1 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A docent-led introduction to works in RMA’s current exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: RMA lists Museum Highlights Tours on select Saturdays, including August 29, 2026, and says both tours and admission are free.
cards.source_title: Current Season at Rollins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The current season asks visitors to secure a tour spot; the listed August 29, 2026 tour begins at 1 p.m.

cards.entity_name: Arte y Café con la Curadora: Pathways 2026
cards.title: Take the Spanish-language Pathways tour
cards.subtitle: Rollins Museum of Art
cards.notes: Reserve a place for the August 18 Spanish-language curator tour, then stay with your group to compare the finalists’ approaches.
cards.short_summary: A Spanish-language curator tour of the Pathways 2026 exhibition.
cards.evidence_claim: RMA schedules an August 18, 2026 Arte y Café con la Curadora tour for Pathways 2026 and states that museum programs are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Current Season at Rollins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Reserve a space through the museum’s tour link; the listed tour starts at 6 p.m. on August 18, 2026.

cards.entity_name: Rollins Museum of Art Outdoor Sculpture Tour
cards.title: Follow the Outdoor Sculpture Tour
cards.subtitle: Rollins campus to The Alfond Inn
cards.notes: Start at the museum’s front steps and follow the self-guided 1.6-mile route with a friend, pausing at each of the seven sculptures.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided campus walk linking seven outdoor sculptures.
cards.evidence_claim: RMA describes a 1.6-mile self-guided outdoor sculpture tour across campus, from its front steps to The Alfond Inn; the museum states admission and programs are free.
cards.source_title: Current Season at Rollins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The route is self-guided and begins at the Rollins Museum of Art front steps; use normal pedestrian care while crossing campus.

cards.entity_name: Rollins Archives and Special Collections Reading Room
cards.title: Research in the Archives Reading Room
cards.subtitle: First floor, Olin Library
cards.notes: Bring a research question or browse eligible collections together; complete the required user registration form and show photo ID before using materials.
cards.short_summary: A public reading room for researching Rollins archival collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins Archives says most collections are open to the Rollins community and general public without restriction and seeks to provide free, open access; its Olin Library reading room is open to the public.
cards.source_title: Rollins Archives and Special Collections Materials Use Policy
cards.access_notes: Researchers must register and present photo ID. The policy lists public reading-room hours as Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4 p.m., excluding most College holidays.

cards.title: Walk Mead Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: 1300 S. Denning Ave., Winter Park
cards.notes: Meet for a slow lap through the gardens, boardwalk, and butterfly garden, then use a bench or picnic table for a no-purchase catch-up.
cards.short_summary: A 47.6-acre public garden with gardens, boardwalk, and trails.
cards.evidence_claim: Mead Botanical Garden states that admission is free to the public; the City of Winter Park identifies its boardwalk, butterfly garden, amphitheater, and bike trail.
cards.source_title: Visit Mead Botanical Garden
cards.access_notes: Free public admission applies to regular visits. Commercial photography and other business activity require City of Winter Park permitting.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For

cards.title: Spread out on Mills Lawn
cards.subtitle: Near Kathleen W. Rollins Hall
cards.notes: Bring a blanket and use the open lawn for reading or laptop work; Olin Library and Skillman Dining Hall are nearby if you need to move indoors.
cards.short_summary: An expansive lawn beside central academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies Mills Lawn as an outdoor extension of campus near Kathleen W. Rollins Hall and notes its proximity to Olin Library and Skillman Dining Hall.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: Outdoor lawn; no reservation or public-access terms are stated on the cited page.

cards.entity_name: Kathleen W. Rollins Hall Picnic Tables
cards.title: Plug in at the Rollins Hall tables
cards.subtitle: Patio outside Kathleen W. Rollins Hall
cards.notes: Set up at a patio table when device power matters: the college specifically documents outlets at the tables outside Kathleen W. Rollins Hall.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor tables with documented electrical outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins states that the patio tables outside Kathleen W. Rollins Hall have outlets for laptop power.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: Outdoor patio tables; no reservation or public-access terms are stated on the cited page.

cards.title: Settle into the Bush Science Center Patio
cards.subtitle: Bush Science Center
cards.notes: Use the landscaped patio for an outdoor work session, then plan your materials before stepping inside; the cited college page describes the patio and its native plants.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped, Spanish-Mediterranean-style science-center patio.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins documents the Bush Science Center Patio as a 2014 renovation addition with travertine marble and landscaping composed almost entirely of native Florida plants.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: Outdoor patio; no reservation or public-access terms are stated on the cited page.

cards.title: Read among Cornell Hall’s archways
cards.subtitle: Cornell Hall
cards.notes: Choose a stone bench in the courtyard for a brief reading block, or use the smaller interior courtyard when you want a more enclosed outdoor setting.
cards.short_summary: Courtyard benches framed by Cornell Hall’s arches and clock tower.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins describes the Cornell Hall Courtyard as having classic archways, a clock tower, stone benches, and a smaller courtyard with an ivy-covered wall.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: Outdoor courtyard; no reservation or public-access terms are stated on the cited page.

cards.title: Take a reading break at Lake Virginia Dock
cards.subtitle: Northeast campus near the Boathouse
cards.notes: Bring compact materials and use the dock for a focused solo session; Rollins places it on the northeast side of campus near the Boathouse.
cards.short_summary: A named dock at the Lake Virginia shoreline.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies a dock on the northeast side of campus near the Boathouse as a location for a solo study session.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: Outdoor dock; use ordinary waterside caution. No reservation or public-access terms are stated on the cited page.

cards.title: Work under the lakeside gazebo
cards.subtitle: Behind Cornell Fine Arts Museum
cards.notes: Take a notebook or reading assignment to the gazebo behind Cornell Fine Arts Museum, where the structure provides cover from sun and rain.
cards.short_summary: A covered lakeside gazebo behind the museum.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies a gazebo behind Cornell Fine Arts Museum that overlooks Lake Virginia and provides shelter from sun and rain.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: Outdoor gazebo; no reservation or public-access terms are stated on the cited page.

cards.title: Use a table on Olin Library Porch
cards.subtitle: Olin Library
cards.notes: Set up at one of the porch tables and chairs for a between-class work block, keeping library resources within immediate walking distance.
cards.short_summary: Wraparound porch seating at the campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins states that Olin Library’s wraparound porch has tables and chairs and is centrally located.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: Outdoor library porch; library/building access and hours should be checked separately.

cards.title: Review notes at Boat Benches
cards.subtitle: Path behind Lakeside Neighborhood
cards.notes: Use the functional Boat Benches along the Lakeside Neighborhood path for a short reading or review session beneath the cypress trees by Lake Virginia.
cards.short_summary: A named public-art seating installation at the lake’s edge.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies Boat Benches, a sculpture by Katherine Tyszko ’11, along the path behind Lakeside Neighborhood under cypress trees at Lake Virginia.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: Outdoor seating installation; no reservation or public-access terms are stated on the cited page.

cards.title: Make a study stop at the Bookstore Patio
cards.subtitle: Outside the Rollins Bookstore
cards.notes: Use the picnic tables outside the bookstore for a study interval, especially when you want a place close to campus and nearby food options.
cards.short_summary: Picnic-table seating outside the campus bookstore.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins documents picnic tables outside the Rollins Bookstore and notes their proximity to on- and off-campus food options.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: Outdoor picnic tables; no reservation or public-access terms are stated on the cited page.

cards.title: Reserve Orlando Hall’s outdoor classroom
cards.subtitle: Courtyard of Orlando Hall
cards.notes: Check the My Rollins app before heading over: Rollins says this outdoor classroom is reservable and can be used between scheduled gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A reservable outdoor classroom in the Orlando Hall courtyard.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies the Orlando Hall Outdoor Classroom in the building’s courtyard and states that it is among study spaces reservable through the My Rollins app.
cards.source_title: 15 Epic Outdoor Study Spots at Rollins
cards.access_notes: The cited Rollins page says this space is reservable through the My Rollins app; check availability before use.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on nearby Winter Park corridors, each with a specific, source-backed reason to stop.

cards.title: Central Park: a downtown green pause
cards.subtitle: Park Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the 11-acre park’s paths, fountains, oak canopy, and Rose Garden; check the city calendar if you want to pair the stop with an event.
cards.short_summary: A civic park embedded in the Park Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City locates Central Park on Park Avenue and identifies its fountains, landscaped planters, oak canopy, Rose Garden, benches, accessible features, and Wi-Fi.
cards.source_title: Central Park — City of Winter Park
cards.access_notes: City-listed location: 251 S. Park Avenue, Winter Park.

cards.entity_name: Charles Hosmer Morse Museum of American Art
cards.title: Morse Museum: Tiffany collection
cards.subtitle: Park Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Plan a gallery visit around the museum’s published hours and ticket rules; allow time for the complimentary cellphone audio tour.
cards.short_summary: A museum stop at Park and Canton avenues.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum is at 445 N. Park Avenue, at Park and Canton avenues, and offers cellphone audio tours for its collection.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit — Charles Hosmer Morse Museum of American Art
cards.access_notes: Published hours: Tuesday–Saturday 9:30 a.m.–4 p.m.; Sunday 1–4 p.m.; check the museum page for exceptions and admission.

cards.title: Casa Feliz: Rogers architecture
cards.subtitle: North Park Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the museum’s tour information before going, then view the Spanish Farmhouse’s exterior, bell tower, roof tiles, gardens, and oak setting.
cards.short_summary: A documented James Gamble Rogers II design on Park Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Casa Feliz identifies itself as a Spanish Farmhouse designed by James Gamble Rogers II and gives its address as 656 N. Park Ave.
cards.source_title: Casa Feliz Historic Home Museum & Venue
cards.access_notes: Physical address: 656 N. Park Ave.; consult Casa Feliz for current historic-tour availability.

cards.title: Scenic Boat Tour: lakes and canals
cards.subtitle: East Morse Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Arrive at the Morse Boulevard dock ready for an hour-long guided tour; review the operator’s current departure and ticket details first.
cards.short_summary: A guided boat-tour departure point on Morse Boulevard.
cards.evidence_claim: The operator lists hour-long guided tours through Winter Park’s lakes and canals from 312 East Morse Blvd.
cards.source_title: Winter Park Scenic Boat Tour
cards.access_notes: The operator lists departures every hour from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.; its page says tours are first come, first served.

cards.title: Farmers’ Market: Saturday browsing
cards.subtitle: New York Avenue and Morse Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Go Saturday morning to browse the city-managed market in Central Park West Meadow; confirm whether a major event has moved it to Seven Oaks Park.
cards.short_summary: A weekly market at the New York–Morse corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says the Saturday Farmers’ Market is held in Central Park West Meadow at New York Avenue and Morse Boulevard, with produce, plants, and baked goods.
cards.source_title: Saturday Farmers’ Market — City of Winter Park
cards.access_notes: Published schedule: Saturdays, 8 a.m.–1 p.m.; the city notes occasional relocations for major events.

cards.title: History Museum: free local exhibits
cards.subtitle: West New England Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Drop in for free educational exhibits about Winter Park and its surrounding area; use the museum’s site to confirm the current exhibit before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A free museum stop in the former freight-depot area.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum states that it tells Winter Park’s story through free educational exhibits and lists its location at 200 W. New England Ave.
cards.source_title: Winter Park History Museum
cards.access_notes: Published hours: Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–2 p.m.; the site notes temporary closures when exhibits change.

cards.title: Heritage Center: oral histories
cards.subtitle: West New England Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Visit the permanent Heritage Collection and timeline, then use the center’s materials to learn about West Winter Park’s African-American community.
cards.short_summary: Free public history and art in Hannibal Square.
cards.evidence_claim: The Heritage Center is at 642 W. New England Avenue and presents a permanent collection of photographs and oral histories of West Winter Park.
cards.source_title: Hannibal Square Heritage Center
cards.access_notes: The center states it is free and open Tuesday–Friday 12–4 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–2 p.m.

cards.title: Shady Park: Hannibal Square memorial
cards.subtitle: West New England Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Pause at the city park beside the Heritage Center to see the Pioneer Memorial and continue on to the center’s exhibits across the adjacent block.
cards.short_summary: A small civic park linked to Hannibal Square history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Shady Park as a historic Hannibal Square site and identifies the adjacent Hannibal Square Heritage Center at 642 W. New England Avenue.
cards.source_title: Shady Park Pioneer Memorial Dedication — City of Winter Park
cards.access_notes: Use the city’s parks information and posted conditions when visiting.

cards.title: Dinky Dock: Lake Virginia access
cards.subtitle: Osceola Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use this compact lakefront park for its fishing pier and water-view stop; follow posted rules for the beach, dock, ramp, and water access.
cards.short_summary: A city lake-access park with a pier and boat ramp.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Dinky Dock Park as a 1.56-acre park with a fishing pier and boat ramp, open year-round from 8 a.m. until dusk.
cards.source_title: Parks — City of Winter Park
cards.access_notes: Published city hours: 8 a.m. until dusk.

cards.title: Kraft Azalea: lakefront garden
cards.subtitle: Alabama Drive corridor
cards.notes: Walk the public garden’s lakefront paths and cypress-shaded grounds during daytime hours; keep the visit simple and respect any reserved-event areas.
cards.short_summary: A city public garden on Lake Maitland.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Kraft Azalea Garden as a 5.22-acre public garden on Lake Maitland that is open year-round from 8 a.m. until dusk.
cards.source_title: Parks — City of Winter Park
cards.access_notes: Published city hours: 8 a.m. until dusk.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Rollins traditions, from first-year welcome rituals to the surprise appearance of the Fox.

cards.title: Serve on SPARC Day
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation tradition
cards.notes: Join the orientation day of service, then use the reflection time to connect the project with the Winter Park community.
cards.short_summary: First-years volunteer with local organizations as part of orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies SPARC Day as an annual orientation tradition in which first-year students volunteer with dozens of local organizations and reflect on their impact.
cards.source_title: Rollins College Traditions
cards.access_notes: Orientation programming for new Rollins students; confirm participation details with Student Affairs.

cards.title: Raise a Candle at Candlewish
cards.subtitle: Fall-semester first-year gathering
cards.notes: Bring your first-year intentions to the fall gathering and take part when the group raises candles around the Fiat Lux theme.
cards.short_summary: A candle-raising welcome ritual centered on community, learning, and Rollins’ motto.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins says first-years gather at the start of each fall semester, receive candles, and raise them to symbolize community, knowledge, and “Fiat Lux.”
cards.source_title: Rollins College Traditions
cards.access_notes: Held during fall welcome programming for first-year students; check orientation communications for details.

cards.title: Wait for Fox Day
cards.subtitle: Surprise spring academic holiday
cards.notes: Watch for the president’s spring announcement; when the Fox appears, pause class plans and join the campus programming.
cards.short_summary: A surprise day off triggered by the president’s placement of the Fox statue.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins states that Fox Day was established in 1956 and that the president cancels College of Liberal Arts classes on a surprise spring day.
cards.source_title: Fox Day at Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Applies to College of Liberal Arts classes on the day selected by the president; programming is announced that day.

cards.title: Spot the Fox on Tars Plaza
cards.subtitle: Fox Day signal at Tars Plaza
cards.notes: Check Tars Plaza on likely spring mornings and photograph the moment only after the president places the Fox statue there.
cards.short_summary: The statue’s appearance is the visual signal that Fox Day has arrived.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins says the president places the Fox statue on Tars Plaza early in the morning to signal Fox Day.
cards.source_title: Fox Day at Rollins College
cards.access_notes: The statue is placed only on Fox Day; do not handle or move it.

cards.title: Pick Up a Fox Day Proclamation
cards.subtitle: President’s office, Fox Day morning
cards.notes: If you are on campus when Fox Day begins, line up outside the president’s office for the day’s proclamation and a donut.
cards.short_summary: The president hands out printed Fox Day proclamations as the celebration starts.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins documents that, on Fox Day, the president hands out Fox Day proclamations and donuts to students lined up outside the president’s office.
cards.source_title: Fox Day at Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Available only on Fox Day and while supplies last; follow on-site directions.

cards.title: Enter the Lip Sync Challenge
cards.subtitle: SGA-connected student-group performance
cards.notes: Form a student-group team, plan a lip-sync-and-dance routine, and follow the event organizer’s participation and audience guidance.
cards.short_summary: Student groups perform choreographed lip-sync and dance routines before a campus audience.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins describes Lip Sync as an annual lip-sync and dance challenge in which dozens of student groups participate.
cards.source_title: Rollins College Traditions
cards.access_notes: Participation and viewing details are set by the Student Government Association for each event.

cards.title: Take a Finals-Eve Breakfast Break
cards.subtitle: Skillman Dining Hall, eve of finals
cards.notes: On the eve of finals, stop by Skillman for the breakfast event and a study break served by faculty, staff, and the president.
cards.short_summary: A free finals-eve breakfast event staffed by Rollins faculty and leaders.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins calls Late Night Breakfast a free eve-of-finals event at Skillman Dining Hall where faculty, staff, and the president serve breakfast foods.
cards.source_title: Rollins College Traditions
cards.access_notes: Scheduled on the eve of finals each semester; confirm event timing and eligibility through campus announcements.

cards.entity_name: Thaddeus & Polly Seymour Acts of Kindness Day
cards.title: Mark Acts of Kindness Day
cards.subtitle: Annual February service tradition
cards.notes: Use the February observance to organize a practical act of service for a neighbor, campus group, or Winter Park community partner.
cards.short_summary: A February day of service honoring Thaddeus and Polly Seymour’s legacy.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins says that since 2020 it has honored Thaddeus and Polly Seymour each February with an annual day for service and commitment to the community.
cards.source_title: Rollins College Traditions
cards.access_notes: Look for February service opportunities announced by Rollins; activity locations vary.

cards.title: Attend Christmas Vespers
cards.subtitle: Knowles Memorial Chapel holiday service
cards.notes: Reserve a ticket for the annual candlelit program of carols and lessons, then arrive through the Chapel’s published entry process.
cards.short_summary: A candlelit Rollins holiday service with a history dating to 1933.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies Christmas Vespers as an annual candlelit College tradition with a history stretching back to 1933.
cards.source_title: Christmas Vespers | Rollins College
cards.access_notes: The published event page lists ticketed admission; Rollins students, faculty, and staff receive complimentary tickets by reservation.

cards.title: Try the Pancake Flip
cards.subtitle: Mills Lawn, orientation week
cards.notes: During orientation week, meet on Mills Lawn and try catching pancakes with fellow new Tars as the event is offered.
cards.short_summary: An orientation-week Mills Lawn activity where new students try to catch pancakes.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins describes the annual Pancake Flip on Mills Lawn during orientation week as a Rollins tradition for new Tars.
cards.source_title: Rollins College: A Year in Photos
cards.access_notes: An orientation-week activity for new students; availability and timing should be confirmed in the current orientation schedule.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Rollins College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that begins on campus, builds in ways to connect, and finishes with nearby Winter Park time.

cards.title: Start with a Lake Virginia walk
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Rollins campus
cards.notes: Walk the lakeside path to get oriented and choose a study view for later; stay on maintained campus paths and follow posted access guidance.
cards.short_summary: A simple first look at Rollins’ lakeside setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies Lake Virginia as a campus feature and describes a lakeside path for jogging and studying by the lake.
cards.source_title: Daily Campus Tours | Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Use maintained campus paths; this card does not assume access to water equipment.

cards.title: Make Olin Library your reset point
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • 1000 Holt Ave.
cards.notes: Stop in to locate research help and a comfortable work setting before the weekend gets busy; check the library site for current building hours.
cards.short_summary: An academic anchor for finding resources and settling in.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins lists Olin Library among its academic resources and identifies it as located on the Rollins College campus in Winter Park.
cards.source_title: Resources at Rollins | Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Access and hours may vary; consult the library before making a late visit.

cards.title: See what’s on view at RMA
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Rollins campus
cards.notes: Choose one current exhibition or the outdoor sculpture tour, then take a few minutes to compare works that catch your attention.
cards.short_summary: A free on-campus art stop with rotating exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins Museum of Art is on the Rollins campus, offers rotating exhibitions and an outdoor sculpture tour, and states that admission is free for all.
cards.source_title: Rollins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The museum lists hours by day; confirm the current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Browse one campus event or organization
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • Rollins online
cards.notes: Use the Rollins Get Involved platform to scan current events and organizations, then save one activity that genuinely fits your interests.
cards.short_summary: A practical way to find the week’s campus connections.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins’ Get Involved platform lets students discover events, find organizations, and track activities and memberships.
cards.source_title: Get Involved | Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Event availability and any event-specific requirements vary; review the listing before attending.

cards.title: Tune in to WPRK
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • Mills Memorial Center
cards.notes: Listen to a WPRK broadcast and, if the station interests you, use its Rollins listing to learn how student and community volunteers participate.
cards.short_summary: A student-directed station serving Rollins and greater Orlando.
cards.evidence_claim: 91.5 WPRK has broadcast since 1952, serves Rollins and greater Orlando, and is directed by student staff with student and community volunteer DJs.
cards.source_title: 91.5 WPRK | Rollins Get Involved
cards.access_notes: Participation is subject to station opportunities and procedures; listening does not require a visit to the studio.

cards.title: Get familiar with The Marketplace
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • Rollins campus
cards.notes: Walk through Rollins’ main dining venue and review the current menu or open locations before deciding on a meal that works for your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining orientation stop before the day begins.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies The Marketplace as the College’s main dining venue.
cards.source_title: Daily Campus Tours | Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Food purchases or meal-plan use may be required; verify current dining availability and menu details.

cards.title: Catch a Rollins game
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • campus athletics venues
cards.notes: Check the athletics calendar, pick a home game that fits, and arrive ready to support the Tars with friends or new hallmates.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission-cost way to experience a campus crowd.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins states that it hosts 21 varsity teams and that admission to all Rollins athletics events is free.
cards.source_title: Community Events | Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Only attend scheduled events; confirm opponent, location, and weather details on the athletics calendar.

cards.title: Ask about a paddleboard checkout
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • Lake Virginia
cards.notes: If you are eligible and conditions permit, ask the Rollins Boathouse about paddleboard checkout and follow all staff direction and water-safety rules.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation option tied to Lake Virginia.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins says paddleboards and boats are available to check out through the Rollins Boathouse for exploring the east side of campus.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation & Intramural Sports | Rollins College
cards.access_notes: Checkout eligibility, equipment availability, weather, and water conditions apply; confirm directly with campus recreation.

cards.title: Take a breather in Central Park
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon • 251 S. Park Ave.
cards.notes: Walk under the oak canopy, use a bench, and look for any city-programmed activity without treating an event as guaranteed on your visit.
cards.short_summary: An 11-acre downtown park beside Park Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winter Park describes Central Park as an 11-acre park on Park Avenue with benches, accessible features, Wi-Fi, fountains, planters, and an oak canopy.
cards.source_title: Central Park | City of Winter Park
cards.access_notes: The city notes that pets are not allowed; follow posted park and event rules.

cards.title: End with a Park Avenue stroll
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening • downtown Winter Park
cards.notes: Walk a short, well-lit section near Central Park, browse storefronts at your own pace, and allow extra time around any active construction blocks.
cards.short_summary: Winter Park’s central downtown street, adjacent to Central Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Winter Park identifies Park Avenue between Webster and Fairbanks avenues as its main street and says pedestrian traffic is maintained during the current refresh project.
cards.source_title: Park Avenue Refresh Project | City of Winter Park
cards.access_notes: A city streetscape refresh has block-by-block closures; use open pedestrian routes and respect barricades.

warnings: Park Avenue is undergoing a city streetscape refresh with moving block closures; use maintained pedestrian routes and confirm current conditions.
